prize_parts.citation: for the invention and realisation of the optical lattice clock, in which a magic-wavelength lattice allows many atoms to be interrogated free of motional shifts, bringing frequency standards to the 10^-18 level

statement.case_for: I move from B007 to B042 as my preferred configuration. The reason is the one I named myself in round 1 as the weak point of my own choice: the attribution for topological insulators. Having read the full exchange, nobody, including me, has shown that Kane, Mele and Molenkamp can be defended as a complete set when Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang (who proposed the HgTe route that Molenkamp tested) and Fu, Moore and Hasan (for three dimensions) stand outside it, and the three-name limit means I cannot repair this. A prize whose credit the committee already expects to be contested is a worse prize than the science deserves. On the science of B042 I now think I underweighted the central idea. The magic-wavelength condition is exactly the kind of simple, general mechanism I look for: choose the trapping wavelength so that the light shift is identical for both clock states, and the lattice stops perturbing the transition while Doppler and recoil shifts vanish and thousands of atoms are interrogated at once. It is a clean physical idea that can be stated in one line and analysed rigorously, it is reproduced in independent laboratories (RIKEN and Tokyo, JILA, PTB, SYRTE, NIST) at about 1e-18, and the credit chain for two names, Katori for the concept and first strontium demonstrations and Ye for taking accuracy, stability and many-body clock physics to the frontier, is short. I still believe that discovering a new class of quantum matter weighs more than a further gain in precision, so this is a choice made on allocation and not a change in my view of which field has the deeper idea. The citation should be drawn around the magic-wavelength lattice and its demonstration, not around clocks or combs in general.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is still the one raised by Danielsson, Lindroth and Olsson: B042 is an invention of an instrument and a precision frontier, and the fundamental-physics results so far (varying constants, ultralight dark matter, gravity) are bounds or prospective, with the millimetre-scale redshift measurement the one clear physical result. Hall and Hansch (2005) and Wineland (2012) already cover adjacent ground, so the citation must not re-reward combs or ion control. Lemonde, Takamoto, Ludlow, Derevianko, and the PTB, NIST and SYRTE teams, and the Al+ ion-clock tradition, have real claims that a two-name credit cannot absorb. Finally, I am a theorist in statistical physics and rely on the AMO members on priority details in the clock literature, which I know only from memory.

responses.point: Lindroth argued that the topological insulator attribution cannot be settled with three names (she would add Hasan and Moore for 3D) and that the lattice clock has a short, well-documented attribution chain, while conceding that the case for B007 would improve if condensed-matter colleagues could settle the credit.
responses.response: I have tried to settle it and cannot. Within three names the choice is between a theory-plus-experiment trio that omits the proposers of the HgTe experiment and a different trio that omits the Kane-Mele Z2 theory, and neither is clearly right. That is why I accept your argument on attribution and move to B042. I do not accept that the lattice clock is merely a measurement achievement; I read the magic-wavelength condition as a real mechanism, and the redshift measurement at millimetre scale is already physics outside what a clock was built for. Where I still differ is that its fundamental-physics reach is mostly bounds so far, and I would like the citation to stay with the mechanism and not promise discoveries it has not delivered.

responses.point: Danielsson called the lattice clock an instrument and a precision frontier rather than a discovery about nature, with no deviation from general relativity or the Standard Model found, but still put it at the head of his list because the attribution is cleanest and the physics is reproduced.
responses.response: I share your caveat and it is the main reason I held back in round 1. Where I now differ is on what counts as the discovery. The lattice clock is not simply a better version of an old instrument. The statement that a particular wavelength makes both clock levels shift identically is a nontrivial result about atoms in light, comparable to a clean theoretical statement that nature allows. The null bounds on drifting constants and dark-matter couplings are real constraints and not nothing, and the redshift across millimetres is a measurement of a relativistic effect in a laboratory. I therefore do not require competitive new bounds before supporting B042, but I would not write a citation that implies a new test of fundamental physics has already succeeded.

responses.point: Eriksson prefers B054 with MacDonald and Jarillo-Herrero only, argues the Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model is a quantitative, falsifiable flat-band prediction confirmed by fast independent reproduction, and says he would put B007 second, not first, because of the 2016 overlap and the missing Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang and Fu credit.
responses.response: We now agree on the B007 problem, and I have moved off it. On B054 I stay with my round-1 view on maturity, and I think the exchange has sharpened it: the continuum model is the clean analysable mechanism I like, but what the experiments found, correlated insulators and superconducting domes, is exactly the part whose origin is unsettled, and the sample-to-sample variation from twist-angle disorder is still large. Fast reproduction shows that the effect is real, not that it is understood, and a prize for the flat-band prediction plus the discovery would be easier to defend after the pairing mechanism has been clarified. The two-name shape, which leaves out Bistritzer, is cleaner than the three-name credit, so I would support it if the committee chose B054, and I move B054 to my alternatives for that reason.

responses.point: Pearce, as chair, asked how large the overlap between the Z2 classification and the 2016 topology prize is in my assessment, and puts weight on a verified, independently reproduced measurement capability.
responses.response: My assessment is that the overlap is real but smaller than the headline suggests. The 2016 prize covered topological phase transitions and Chern-type invariants in systems with broken time-reversal symmetry, the TKNN and Haldane line. Z2 topology protected by time-reversal symmetry, with helical edge states, is a separate classification. I would not call it duplication. The difficulty is not overlap, it is that the credited set is incomplete and the three-name limit prevents repair, and a conceptual precedent of that kind compounds it. I agree with your weighting of independently verified capability, which is what the lattice clock offers.

uncertainties: Whether the committee has verified the primary literature on who first proposed the magic-wavelength lattice (Katori and collaborators, and the earlier theory on magic wavelengths) so that the two-name credit is exact; my own knowledge of the priority record is from memory.
Whether the citation can be drawn tightly enough around the magic-wavelength lattice to avoid re-rewarding the 2005 comb prize and the 2012 ion-control prize.
Whether a later prize on topological insulators remains possible with a defensible set of names, and whether the committee would regret closing the window through this year's choice.
Whether the fundamental-physics payoff of lattice clocks (varying constants, dark matter, gravity) will turn from bounds into a positive result, which would strengthen the case in hindsight.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for any shortlisted candidate. I have no known collaboration with Katori, Ye, Kane, Mele, Molenkamp, MacDonald or Jarillo-Herrero. I work in the same Gothenburg physics environment as colleagues Johansson and Olsson, which is an institutional fact and not a recusal issue for B042. I have no new disclosure since round 1.
